name: array
description: Problems where the primary data structure is an indexed collection of values.
examples: find an element in an array
include_when: The problem primarily operates on an array.
The input contains an indexed sequence of values and array operations are central to the solution.

name: string
description: Problems where the primary data structure is a sequence of characters.
include_when: The problem primarily operates on strings or sequences of characters.
Character-level operations are central to solving the problem.

name: linked list
description: Problems involving nodes connected through next or previous references.
include_when: The problem uses linked-list nodes connected through references.
Traversal, modification, or comparison of linked-list nodes is central to the solution.

name: tree
description: Problems involving hierarchical structures made of nodes connected by parent-child relationships.
include_when: The problem represents data using a tree or hierarchical node structure.
Parent-child relationships are central to the solution.

name: graph
description: Problems involving vertices connected through edges or transitions.
include_when: The problem models entities as vertices connected by edges or transitions.
Relationships or paths between nodes are central to the problem.

name: stack
description: Problems where last-in-first-out behavior is central to the solution.
include_when: A last-in-first-out data structure is central to the intended solution.
The solution repeatedly pushes and pops elements while maintaining stack order.

name: queue
description: Problems where first-in-first-out processing is central.
include_when: First-in-first-out processing is central to the intended solution.
A queue is used to process states or elements in arrival order.

name: hashing
description: Using hash tables, maps, or sets for fast lookup, membership testing, grouping, or counting.
include_when: Fast lookup, membership testing, counting, or mapping is central to the intended solution.
A hash map or hash set significantly reduces the required time complexity.

name: dynamic programming
description: Solving a problem by defining states for subproblems and reusing solutions to overlapping subproblems.
include_when: The intended solution defines states representing subproblems and reuses previously computed results.
Overlapping subproblems and state transitions are central to the solution.

name: greedy
description: Making a locally optimal choice at each step with the goal of obtaining a globally optimal result.
include_when: The intended solution repeatedly makes locally optimal choices without needing to reconsider previous decisions.
The local-choice strategy can be justified as producing an optimal global result.

name: divide and conquer
description: Breaking a problem into smaller subproblems, solving them independently or recursively, and combining the results.
include_when: The intended solution divides the input into smaller parts, solves those parts, and combines their results.
Independent recursive subproblems form the main structure of the algorithm.

name: backtracking
description: Exploring possible choices incrementally and undoing choices when they cannot lead to a valid solution.
include_when: The solution explores multiple possible choices and reverses a choice when continuing from it is no longer useful or valid.
The algorithm searches a decision tree and restores state after recursive exploration.

name: sorting
description: Reordering values to expose useful relationships or make another algorithm possible.
include_when: Sorting is an important part of the intended solution.
Reordering the input exposes relationships or enables an efficient subsequent technique.

name: binary search
description: Repeatedly reducing an ordered search space by comparing a target with a middle position.
include_when: The intended solution repeatedly halves an ordered search space.
The algorithm uses a monotonic or sorted property to eliminate roughly half of the candidates at each step.

name: binary search on answer
description: Searching over possible answer values when feasibility changes monotonically.
examples: check whether an answer is possible
include_when: The search space consists of possible answer values rather than input positions.
A feasibility predicate changes monotonically as the candidate answer changes.

name: subarray
description: A contiguous portion of an array.
include_when: The problem selects, examines, counts, or optimizes over a contiguous segment of an array.
All elements between two chosen boundaries belong to the considered sequence.

name: subsequence
description: A sequence formed by deleting zero or more elements while preserving the relative order of the remaining elements.
examples: nums[i1], nums[i2], nums[i3] where i1 < i2 < i3
include_when: The problem explicitly asks for or constructs a subsequence: a sequence formed by selecting elements while preserving their relative order.
The selected elements themselves form the central object, constraint, or output of the problem.
The solution depends on properties of the selected subsequence as a sequence.
Do not assign this concept merely because some elements are skipped.
Do not assign this concept merely because a dynamic programming solution has take/skip choices.

name: substring
description: A contiguous portion of a string.
include_when: The problem considers a contiguous range of characters in a string.
Characters between two string indices must remain together.

name: subsequence of string
description: A sequence of characters formed by deleting characters while preserving their relative order.
examples: check whether one string is a subsequence of another
include_when: Characters may be skipped while their original relative order must remain unchanged.
The problem asks whether or how one string can be obtained as a subsequence of another.

name: prefix
description: A portion of an array or string beginning at the first element or character.
include_when: A segment begins at the first element or first character.
The solution reasons about the portion of the input from index 0 through a variable endpoint.

name: suffix
description: A portion of an array or string extending from a chosen position to the end.
include_when: A segment extends from some position to the final element or character.
The solution reasons about the remaining portion of the input after a chosen position.

name: prefix sum
description: A cumulative representation that stores the sum of values from the beginning up to each position.
include_when: Cumulative sums from the start are used to answer range-sum or balance queries efficiently.
The solution relies on differences between prefix sums.

name: suffix sum
description: A cumulative representation that stores the sum of values from each position through the end.
examples: sum of all elements after an index
include_when: Cumulative sums from each position to the end are used in the intended solution.
The solution needs efficient computation of sums over suffixes or elements to the right of an index.

name: two pointers
description: Using two indices that move through a sequence to reduce the search space or maintain a relationship between positions.
examples: move two pointers toward each other
include_when: Two indices are actively maintained and moved according to a rule during the main algorithm.
The movement of two pointers is central to reducing the search space or maintaining a relationship.

name: sliding window
description: Maintaining a contiguous range with left and right boundaries that move through an array or string.
include_when: The algorithm maintains a contiguous active window with left and right boundaries.
The window expands, shrinks, or moves while maintaining a condition over the current range.

name: index relationship
description: Problems where the solution depends on a mathematical or positional relationship between indices.
include_when: A mathematical or positional relationship between indices is central to the solution.
The exact positions or differences between positions matter independently of the values alone.

name: mirror index
description: Two positions that are symmetric around the center of a sequence, commonly represented by i and n-1-i.
include_when: The solution compares or relates positions symmetric around the center.
The relationship i and n-1-i, or an equivalent mirror relationship, is central to the problem.
The problem compares elements from opposite ends of a sequence as corresponding positions.
Do not assign this concept merely because two arbitrary positions are compared.

name: adjacent indices
description: Problems involving neighboring positions such as i and i+1 or i and i-1.
include_when: The solution specifically depends on neighboring or consecutive positions.
The relationship between i and i+1 or i and i-1 is important to the condition or transition.

name: index distance
description: Problems where the difference or distance between two indices is part of the condition or objective.
include_when: The difference, gap, or distance between two indices is explicitly used in the condition.
The problem asks to maximize, minimize, bound, or otherwise reason about index distance.

name: two indices
description: Problems where selecting, comparing, or relating two positions in a sequence is central to the solution.
include_when: The core problem requires selecting or reasoning about a pair of positions.
The relationship between two indices is central even if a literal two-pointer technique is not used.

name: three indices
description: Problems where relationships among three positions or elements are central to the solution.
include_when: The core condition or objective involves three distinct indices or elements.
The ordering or relationship among i, j, and k is important to the solution.

name: take or skip
description: A decision pattern where the current element is either selected or skipped, producing alternative state transitions.
examples: take current element or move on
include_when: The central problem pattern is deciding whether to select/use an item or skip it.
The take/skip decision directly represents the reusable problem structure.
Different choices of taking or skipping items determine the main optimization or counting recurrence.
Do not assign this concept merely because a DP recurrence chooses between two previously computed states.

name: state transition
description: A rule describing how the current state is derived from one or more previously computed states.
include_when: The specific transition structure is itself a meaningful reusable pattern that distinguishes the problem from ordinary dynamic programming.
The problem relies on a notable state-transition relationship that is useful as a searchable characteristic.
Do not assign this concept merely because a dynamic programming solution contains recurrence equations.

name: one dimensional dp
description: Dynamic programming where the state is represented primarily by one dimension.
include_when: The primary DP state can be represented with one varying dimension.
The solution mainly uses values such as dp[i] rather than a grid or matrix of states.

name: two dimensional dp
description: Dynamic programming where the state depends on two dimensions such as two indices or quantities.
include_when: The DP state requires two independent dimensions.
The solution naturally uses a table such as dp[i][j] where both dimensions carry meaningful state information.

name: subsequence dp
description: Dynamic programming where states represent properties, choices, or optimizations over subsequences.
examples: state based on previous selected element
include_when: The DP state represents a property or optimization of a subsequence.
The solution makes ordered selection decisions among elements while preserving relative order.

name: interval dp
description: Dynamic programming where states represent contiguous intervals and transitions split, expand, or shrink those intervals.
examples: solve a range from l to r
include_when: The DP state represents a contiguous interval using boundaries such as l and r.
Transitions operate by splitting, shrinking, or combining intervals.

name: partition dp
description: Dynamic programming where a sequence, set, or range is divided into smaller parts and the best combination is computed.
include_when: The solution divides a sequence, range, or set into multiple parts.
DP states represent different partition boundaries or numbers of groups.

name: monotonic stack
description: A stack maintained in increasing or decreasing order to efficiently resolve relationships between elements.
examples: pop while current value is greater
find nearest larger or smaller value
include_when: The stack is deliberately maintained in monotonic increasing or decreasing order.
Elements are popped based on comparisons with the current element to find nearest greater or smaller relationships.

name: next greater element
description: Finding the first element to the right that is greater than the current element.
aliases: first greater element to the right
examples: find the next value greater than nums[i]
scan from right to left with a stack
include_when: For each element, the problem asks for or depends on the nearest or first greater element to its right.
The next greater relationship is central even if another implementation is possible.

name: previous greater element
description: Finding the nearest element to the left that is greater than the current element.
include_when: The problem asks for or depends on the nearest greater element to the left of each relevant element.

name: next smaller element
description: Finding the first element to the right that is smaller than the current element.
aliases: first smaller element to the right
examples: find the next value smaller than nums[i]
include_when: The problem asks for or depends on the nearest or first smaller element to the right.

name: previous smaller element
description: Finding the nearest element to the left that is smaller than the current element.
include_when: The problem asks for or depends on the nearest smaller element to the left.

name: frequency counting
description: Counting how often values, characters, or categories occur and using those counts to solve a problem.
include_when: Counts or frequencies of values or characters are directly used in the solution.
The number of occurrences of an item affects the condition, output, or state.

name: duplicate detection
description: Determining whether a value, element, or state appears more than once.
include_when: The problem requires determining whether a value, character, or state has appeared previously.
Repeated occurrences or uniqueness are central to the condition.

name: complement lookup
description: Searching for a value that complements the current value to satisfy a target equation or condition.
examples: find the number needed to reach target
include_when: For a current value, the solution computes or reasons about the specific complementary value needed to satisfy a target condition.
The problem can be solved by looking up the value needed to pair with the current value.

name: palindrome
description: A sequence or string that remains the same when read from both directions.
aliases: reads the same forwards and backwards
include_when: The problem asks whether a sequence reads the same forwards and backwards.
Matching symmetric elements or characters is central to the solution.

name: symmetry
description: A problem where equivalent or related elements, positions, or states occur in symmetric arrangements.
include_when: The problem contains a meaningful structural symmetry between two or more sides, regions, positions, or states.
The solution exploits a reflection or mirrored relationship.

name: optimization objective
description: A problem objective involving minimizing or maximizing a value, cost, length, count, score, or number of operations.
include_when: The problem explicitly asks for an optimization objective such as minimum cost, maximum value, shortest length, or best possible result.
The objective itself is a meaningful searchable characteristic of the problem.
Do not assign this concept merely because the solution computes a maximum or minimum internally.

name: maximize value
description: The goal is to maximize a numerical value, score, sum, profit, capacity, or similar quantity.
include_when: The optimization objective is explicitly to maximize a numerical quantity.
Maximizing that quantity is a central part of the problem's formulation rather than merely describing the meaning of words such as longest, largest, or greatest.

name: minimize value
description: The goal is to minimize a numerical value, cost, distance, score, or similar quantity.
include_when: The required answer is the smallest possible value, cost, distance, or similar quantity.

name: maximize count
description: The goal is to maximize the number of selected items, valid operations, elements, or successful outcomes.
examples: select the maximum number of intervals
include_when: The problem explicitly asks to maximize the number of selected items, operations, groups, or valid configurations.
The quantity being maximized is a count and this count is central to the problem objective.
Do not assign this concept merely because the answer is a maximum length or maximum value.

name: minimize count
description: The goal is to minimize the number of selected items, operations, steps, or counted actions.
include_when: The objective is to use the fewest possible operations, elements, steps, jumps, or other counted actions.

name: count number of ways
description: The task is to count how many distinct valid ways, configurations, paths, or choices exist.
examples: number of ways to reach target
include_when: The required answer is the number of distinct valid solutions, paths, choices, or configurations.
The problem asks how many ways something can be achieved rather than asking for one solution.

name: reachability
description: Determining whether a state, position, node, or target can be reached from a starting state.
examples: can we reach the last index?
include_when: The main question is whether a particular state, node, position, or target is reachable.
The answer is fundamentally a yes/no or feasibility question about reaching a target.

name: connectivity
description: Determining which vertices, components, or regions are connected through edges or valid transitions.
examples: determine whether two nodes are connected
include_when: The problem asks which nodes, cells, or components belong to the same connected region.
Connectivity through edges, adjacency, or valid transitions is central to the solution.

name: shortest path
description: Finding the minimum-cost, minimum-distance, or minimum-edge path between states or vertices.
include_when: The objective is to find a path with minimum distance, cost, weight, or number of edges.
Path length or accumulated path cost is explicitly minimized.

name: graph traversal
description: Systematically visiting vertices and edges to explore a graph.
include_when: The solution systematically visits graph vertices or edges to explore reachable states.
Traversal order rather than direct mathematical computation is central to the solution.

name: depth first search
description: Exploring one branch or path as deeply as possible before backtracking.
include_when: The intended solution explores one branch deeply before exploring sibling branches.
DFS is used as the primary traversal strategy for a graph, tree, or state space.

name: breadth first search
description: Exploring states level by level using a queue.
examples: process nodes by distance from source
include_when: The solution explores nodes or states level by level.
A queue is used to process states in order of their distance or depth from a starting state.

name: tree traversal
description: Visiting tree nodes using an organized traversal such as preorder, inorder, postorder, or level order.
include_when: Systematically visiting tree nodes is central to the solution.
The solution uses preorder, inorder, postorder, or level-order traversal.

name: binary tree
description: A tree where each node has at most two children.
include_when: The input structure is a binary tree where each node has at most two children.

name: binary search tree
description: A binary tree organized so values in the left subtree are smaller and values in the right subtree are larger according to the BST ordering rule.
examples: search for a value in a BST
include_when: The tree satisfies binary-search ordering properties.
The solution exploits the fact that values are ordered relative to the root and subtrees.

name: prefix matching
description: Problems where matching or comparing prefixes of strings is central to the solution.
examples: check whether one string starts with another
include_when: The problem compares, searches, or constructs prefixes of one or more strings.
A shared starting sequence or prefix condition is central to the solution.

name: modular arithmetic
description: Using properties of remainders and modular operations to solve a problem.
include_when: Properties of remainders or modular equivalence are central to the reasoning.
The solution relies on modulo operations to establish the required condition or compute the answer.

name: mathematics
description: Problems whose primary reasoning relies on mathematical properties, formulas, arithmetic, number theory, combinatorics, or mathematical transformations.
include_when: Mathematical properties or derivations are the primary source of the solution.
The problem can be solved mainly through arithmetic, algebra, number theory, geometry, or combinatorial reasoning rather than a major data-structure technique.

name: greatest common divisor
description: Problems involving the greatest common divisor of integers or relationships derived from it.
include_when: The solution explicitly computes or relies on the greatest common divisor of numbers.
Divisibility relationships derived from the GCD are central to the problem.

name: prime factorization
description: Breaking an integer into its prime factors and using those factors to reason about the problem.
include_when: The intended solution depends on decomposing integers into prime factors.
Properties of prime divisors determine the answer or enable the main optimization.

name: combinatorics
description: Using counting principles, permutations, combinations, or arrangements to determine the number of possible configurations.
include_when: The main reasoning uses counting principles, combinations, permutations, or arrangements.
The number of possible configurations can be derived mathematically rather than by explicitly enumerating all of them.

name: bit manipulation
description: Using binary representations and bitwise operations such as AND, OR, XOR, shifts, and masks.
include_when: Bitwise operations or binary representations are central to the intended solution.
Operations such as AND, OR, XOR, shifting, or masking are used to represent or transform state.

name: set or subset
description: Problems involving selecting any collection of elements regardless of their original order.
include_when: The problem asks to select any collection of elements without requiring the original order to be preserved.
The solution reasons about membership in a subset rather than a contiguous range or ordered subsequence.

name: permutation
description: Problems involving rearrangements where the order of all selected elements matters.
include_when: The problem involves rearranging a collection into different possible orders.
The exact ordering of all selected elements matters to the solution.

name: interval
description: Problems representing ranges with start and end points and reasoning about overlap, ordering, or containment.
include_when: The input or state is naturally represented as ranges with start and end boundaries.
Overlap, containment, ordering, or relationships between intervals are central to the solution.

name: merge intervals
description: Sorting intervals and combining overlapping or connected intervals.
include_when: The task requires combining overlapping or connected intervals into larger ranges.
Sorting intervals and merging ranges is central to the intended solution.

name: fast and slow pointers
description: Using two pointers that move at different speeds to detect cycles, find middle positions, or compare positions separated by a changing distance.
examples: slow moves one step while fast moves two steps
detect a cycle in a linked list
find the middle of a linked list
include_when: The intended solution uses two pointers that move at different speeds.
One pointer advances faster than another to detect cycles, find a midpoint, or establish a positional relationship.

name: cycle detection
description: Determining whether repeatedly following transitions eventually revisits a previously visited state or forms a cycle.
include_when: The problem asks whether a cycle exists or requires detecting repeated states caused by transitions.
The intended solution identifies a loop in a linked list, graph, or repeated-state process.

name: grid dp
description: Dynamic programming over cells of a grid where each cell's state depends on previously processed neighboring cells.
examples: number of paths to a cell
minimum path cost in a grid
include_when: The problem is represented as a grid or matrix and the intended solution computes a DP state for individual cells.
A cell's answer depends on previously computed neighboring cells or directions.

name: bitmask
description: Using individual bits of an integer as boolean flags to represent membership, selections, or states.
examples: use bits to represent selected elements
include_when: Individual bits represent membership, choices, flags, or subsets.
Bitwise operations are used to encode multiple boolean states into an integer.

name: XOR
description: Using exclusive OR properties to compare, cancel, combine, or isolate binary states or values.
examples: use XOR to find a unique element
include_when: XOR properties are central to deriving the solution.
Equal values cancel through XOR or XOR is used to represent a binary state relationship.

name: trie
description: A prefix tree where paths represent sequences of characters or symbols and shared prefixes are stored together.
examples: insert a word character by character
include_when: The intended solution stores strings by their prefixes in a trie or prefix tree.
Efficient prefix insertion, search, or comparison is central to the algorithm.

name: number theory
description: Problems based on properties of integers such as divisibility, primes, factors, greatest common divisors, or arithmetic structure.
include_when: The main solution depends on structural properties of integers rather than ordinary arithmetic alone.
Divisibility, primes, factors, GCD, LCM, or related integer properties drive the solution.

name: union find
description: A disjoint-set data structure used to maintain dynamically changing connected components.
include_when: The intended solution maintains sets of connected components using union and find operations.
The problem repeatedly merges groups and queries whether elements belong to the same component.

name: feasibility check
description: Determining whether a candidate value, configuration, or answer satisfies all required constraints.
examples: check whether capacity X is sufficient
test whether a candidate schedule is valid
determine whether a target can be achieved
include_when: The algorithm repeatedly tests whether a candidate solution or answer is valid or achievable.
A feasibility predicate is used to eliminate impossible candidates or search for an optimum.

name: parentheses matching
description: Using a stack or equivalent state tracking to determine whether opening and closing parentheses or brackets are properly matched and nested.
examples: push opening brackets and match them with closing brackets
include_when: The problem requires determining whether brackets or parentheses are properly balanced, matched, or nested.
The solution pairs opening symbols with corresponding closing symbols.

name: interval scheduling
description: Selecting or arranging intervals to maximize compatible intervals or satisfy scheduling constraints.
examples: select the maximum number of non-overlapping intervals
choose meetings that do not conflict
include_when: The problem requires selecting or scheduling intervals subject to overlap or compatibility constraints.
The solution reasons about which intervals can coexist without conflict.

name: merge sort
description: A sorting technique that recursively divides an array into halves, sorts each half, and merges the sorted halves.
examples: split array into left and right halves
include_when: The intended algorithm recursively divides the array and merges sorted subarrays.
The merge operation is central to the solution.

name: recursion
description: A technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself on smaller or simpler instances.
examples: solve left subtree and right subtree recursively
include_when: The intended or canonical solution is fundamentally recursive and the recursive structure is a meaningful searchable characteristic.
Recursion is central to the solution rather than merely an alternative implementation.
Do not assign recursion simply because dynamic programming can be expressed using recursive memoization.

name: combination
description: Selecting a collection of elements where the order of selection does not matter.
include_when: The problem asks for or constructs selections where order does not matter.
The same set of selected elements represents the same solution regardless of selection order.

name: sorted array
description: An array whose elements are arranged in non-decreasing or otherwise specified sorted order.
examples: nums is sorted in ascending order
include_when: The input is explicitly sorted or the intended solution first sorts it and then relies on that ordering.
Ordered values are essential to the logic of the solution.

name: increasing subsequence
description: A subsequence in which each selected element is greater than the previous selected element.
include_when: The selected elements must remain in original order and satisfy a strictly increasing value relationship.
The problem asks for, counts, or optimizes an increasing subsequence.

name: longest common subsequence
description: Finding the longest sequence that appears as a subsequence in two sequences while preserving relative order.
examples: dp[i][j] for prefixes of two strings
characters appear in both strings in the same order
include_when: The problem asks for the longest subsequence common to two sequences or strings.
The relative order must be preserved in both input sequences.

name: suffix matching
description: Problems where suffixes of strings or sequences are compared, searched, or required to match.
examples: check whether one string ends with another
include_when: The problem compares or searches suffixes of strings or sequences.
A matching ending segment is central to the condition or result.

name: cyclic pattern
description: A repeating or wraparound relationship where positions or values cycle back to the beginning after reaching an endpoint.
include_when: The solution treats the beginning and end as connected or uses repeating positions.
Indices or states wrap around after reaching a boundary.

name: three sum
description: Finding three elements or indices whose values satisfy a target sum or related three-element condition.
examples: find three numbers whose sum is zero
include_when: The problem requires selecting three elements or indices and reasoning about their combined values.
A three-element sum or equivalent three-element relationship is central to the problem.

name: maximize length
description: The problem asks for the maximum possible length of a valid sequence, substring, subsequence, prefix, or other structure.
include_when: The problem explicitly asks to maximize the length of a structure.
The length being maximized is a central objective of the problem.
Do not assign this concept merely because the answer happens to be a length.
